1. spectacle-open (define): opening Winning at the Olympics is the pinnacle of physical achievement for any athlete., closing As modelers, we have been tasked with predicting the outcome of the 2028 Summer Olympics held in Los Angeles, United States., Stored units 1-2 merged (Delta -1): the spectacle opening and the modeler task statement; block 5 is a one-sentence paragraph with a single terminator.

2. task-and-tobit (define): opening Olympic medal data exhibits censorship in the form of zero inflation, so we first consider a Tobit Model that considers random noise and unobserved random effects, optimized with a Maximum Likelihood Estimate., closing The Mixed Linear Effects Model is then used to perform a Negative Binomial Regression based on the predictors, as well as a Probit Regression in the low-performing cluster to determine probability of earning 0 medals., Stored units 3-4 merged: the Tobit start, the heteroscedasticity finding, the DBSCAN clustering and the hurdle probit all sit in this one 133-word block.

3. rank-and-first-medal (interpret): opening We predicted the Top 3 (in gold count) countries in the 2028 Summer Olympics to be the United States (48), Germany (28), and China (25), each with a 95% confidence interval range of around 30., closing Finally, our model also predicts that the countries that will earn their first Olympic medal in 2028 are Angola and Saar, with odds of 32.54% and 40.08%, respectively., Stored unit 5; the top three gold counts with 95% intervals, the largest rank movements and the Angola and Saar first-medal odds.

4. sport-scores (interpret): opening After analyzing the dynamics of the rankings, we wanted to understand the impact of events and sports on the rankings., closing Then, through Singular Value Decomposition, Sport-Point Efficiency, and Revealed Comparative Advantage, we were able to understand the influence sports and events had on the ranking of various countries., Stored unit 6; the 6-3-2 point system and the SVD, SPE and RCA machinery.

5. coach-screen (interpret): opening We also analyzed past performances at the Games to identify possible instances of the great coach effect, or the influence of a great coach in leading teams to anomalous successes., closing We found that the 1976 Romanian Handball team, the 2008 Canadian trampolining team, and the 2000 Russian diving team were the most likely to have experienced the great coach effect., Stored unit 7; the moving-average time series screen and the three most likely great-coach segments.

6. coach-advice (interpret): opening By using a contribution metric, we used the same model to find the country-sport pairs where the great coach effect was likely to have made the greatest impact on the country’s performance., closing Based on their performances under great coaches, these investments could lead to up to 20 points for Russia, 14 points for China, and 6.8 points for Hungary., Stored unit 8 part; the contribution metric, the 100% Swedish and American stretches and the Russia, China and Hungary advice.

7. close (interpret): opening All of these results were cross-referenced with historical Olympic coaches, and many of our findings lined up with the leadership of coaches that may be considered great., closing … e are a multitude of benefits in this research—such as understanding how to best allocate resources—but more than that, just as the Games represent the human desire for unity in excellence, these models represent our fundamental desire to understand the world., Stored unit 8 part; the cross-reference with historical coaches and the closing reflection; the closing quote falls back to the whole block-12 sentence.

heading: 6 Strengths and Weaknesses
note:

1. mixed-strength (interpret): opening A strength of our model is that, by implementing mixed effects and clusters, it is able to account for various levels of unobserved random effects that can influence medal counts., closing In addition, our model appropriately accounts for the zero-inflation/censoring of Olympic medal data by using a Hurdle model approach with a probit regression to find probability of earning 0 medals or not., Stored unit 1; the mixed-effects and cluster strength plus the hurdle handling of zero inflation.

2. fit-weakness (limit): opening One weakness about this model is it’s fit., closing Some approach that accounts for the heteroscedasticity error would improve the model significantly., Stored unit 2; the non-converging likelihood, the subpar AIC and BIC and the abandoned Hamiltonian Monte Carlo attempt.

4. manual-weakness (limit): opening The main weakness of our model is that there is no way to determine whether anomalous performances were due to the great coach effect or any number of outside influences without manually comparing our findings to historical great coaches., closing Because of the limited data, this is inevitable., Stored unit 4; the manual cross-check requirement and the data limitation.
